title: Introduce nonce-bound service auth and residency-opaque headers
author: Ethan Patel
description:
Context: Recent incident analysis (ENG-2219) showed replay windows and header leakage allowed cross-operator correlation of residency assertions. This PR implements two complementary defenses: 1) nonce-bound service authentication: session- and request-level nonces are bound into KMS envelopes and RBAC v2 decision checks so any replayed KMS token or operator lease that does not present a matching nonce is rejected; 2) residency-opaque headers: residency assertions are encoded as opaque, peppered hashes when forwarded to downstream services to avoid exposing raw region identifiers in logs or telemetry while preserving verifiability at the gateway.

Goals: reduce auditable replay risk, limit residency attribute exposure in transit, and add minimal compatibility shims for Private/VPC deployments.

What this PR does: - Implements a nonce middleware that issues, validates, and caches short-lived nonces tied to a service session. Nonces are emitted into KMS envelope metadata and into a per-request audit token. - Extends KMS proxy to include nonce in encryption context and validate nonce signature on unwrap as an additional gate. - Adds an RBAC v2 policy check (opt-in per-role) that requires nonce binding for operator leases and ephemeral roles. This prevents elevation via replayed operator tokens. - Introduces a ResidencyOpaqueHeader generator (X-Residency-Opaque) that produces a peppered HMAC over the residency claim; the raw claim remains available to the policy engine in the control plane but downstream routes only see the opaque value. - Adds audit-replay-detector that records nonce sequence numbers in an append-only index and rejects duplicates within a configured window; metrics exported: audit.replay.detected, nonce.cache.hits/misses, residency.header.generated. - Updates docs and migration notes for operators running Private installer: toggles to enable/disable header obfuscation and the RBAC-Nonce requirement are in configuration with safe defaults (disabled for older clusters).

Checklist: - [x] Nonce middleware implementation and unit tests - [x] KMS envelope changes and integration tests - [x] RBAC v2 opt-in validator and policy examples - [x] Audit replay detector and metrics - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] Backward compatibility gates for older control planes

Compatibility/migration: Enabled behind feature flag `security.nonce_binding.v1` and `security.residency_opaque_headers`. Operators upgrading from <2024.8 should coordinate: turn on flags in canary first. Migration docs: docs/security/nonce-auth.md.

Related: ENG-2219, SEC-104, SUP-342.

Notes: design intentionally avoids changing user-visible API payloads except for adding an optional X-Residency-Opaque header (downstream compatible); nonces are internal tokens and never exposed to customer request bodies.

feat(kms): include nonce in encryption context and unwrap-time verification
feat(rbac): add nonce-requirement policy check and examples

review_comments: Kara Nguyen: Please add metrics for nonce issuance rate and an opt-out config at the namespace level — otherwise we risk noisy defaults in multi-tenant control planes.
Ethan Patel: Added metrics (audit.nonce.issued) and added namespace opt-out in the second patch — see auth/middleware/nonce_auth.go lines 120-153.
Jamal Rivers: Can we ensure that the KMS providers that don't support arbitrary encryption context keys degrade gracefully? Suggest a compatibility shim in kms/proxy.
Ethan Patel: KMS shim added — it falls back to signed assertion header when encryption context is unsupported. Documented in migration notes.
Sofie Martin: Tests are failing intermittently on CI e2e with Private installer; looks like timing on cache eviction. Please add deterministic sleeps or configurable TTL for tests.
Ethan Patel: Fixed flakiness by making test TTL configurable and reducing reliance on wall-clock sleeps; added deterministic clock in tests.
Kara Nguyen: LGTM after minor doc nits resolved.
release_notes: Security: Add optional nonce-bound service authentication and residency-opaque headers. Feature guarded behind 'security.nonce_binding.v1' and 'security.residency_opaque_headers'. Operators should read docs/security/nonce-auth.md for upgrade steps.
notes_for_ops: Feature flags default to disabled for existing clusters. Recommended rollout: enable feature flags in canary cluster, monitor metrics audit.replay.detected and audit.nonce.issued, then enable for control plane. Private deployments must update installer >= 2024.11 to pick up KMS shim. See docs/security/nonce-auth.md for commands.
short_summary: Adds nonce binding to service auth, KMS envelope support, an RBAC v2 opt-in check to prevent replay elevation, and opaque residency headers to avoid region leakage.
impact_assessment: Low-risk opt-in security hardening. No breaking changes when feature flags are off. Slight CPU overhead for HMAC generation on high-throughput gateways; metric budget and batching recommended.
qa_notes: Integration tests cover KMS fallback behavior, RBAC policy enforcement, and header generation. Manual QA: simulate replay using recorded envelope and verify rejection, confirm opaque header present for routed HTTP calls when flag enabled.
